Consider a relational table with a single record for each registered student with the following attributes.

1. Registration_Number: Unique registration number for each registered student
2. UID: Unique Identity number, unique at the national level for each citizen
3. BankAccount_Number: Unique account number at the bank. A student can have multiple accounts or joint accounts. This attributes stores the primary account number
4. Name: Name of the Student
5. Hostel_Room: Room number of the hostel

Which of the following options is INCORRECT?

options.B: Registration_Number can be a primary key
options.C: UID is a candidate key if all students are from the same country
options.D: If [latex]S[/latex] is a superkey such that [latex]\text{S}\cap \text{UID}[/latex] is NULL then [latex]\text{S}\cup \text{UID}[/latex] is also a superkey

questions.explanation:
A joint account can be the primary account of more than one student, so BankAccount_Number need not be unique [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] it is not a candidate key. Option 1 is INCORRECT.

- Registration_Number is unique [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] can be primary key.
- UID is unique within a country.
- Adding attributes to a super key keeps it a super key.

Answer: BankAccount_Number is a candidate key

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Two Phase Locking (2PL) protocol is/are TRUE?

options.B: With 2PL, a transaction always locks the data item being read or written just before every operation and always releases the lock just after the operation
options.C: With 2PL, once a lock is released on any data item inside a transaction, no more locks on any data item can be obtained inside that transaction

questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- 2PL guarantees conflict serializability, so it permits only serializable schedules [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Locking just before each operation and releasing just after violates 2PL (a release followed by a new lock) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- Growing phase then shrinking phase: once a lock is released, no new lock can be acquired [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE (definition).
- Deadlock is possible: T1 locks A, T2 locks B, then each waits for the other [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Options 1, 3 and 4

questions.question:
Consider a linear list based directory implementation in a file system. Each directory is a list of nodes, where each node contains the file name along with the file metadata, such as the list of pointers to the data blocks. Consider a given directory foo.

Which of the following operations will necessarily require a full scan of foo for successful completion?

options.A: Creation of a new file in foo
options.B: Deletion of an existing file from foo
options.C: Renaming of an existing file in foo
options.D: Opening of an existing file in foo

questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- Create: must check that no file with that name already exists [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] scan the whole list.
- Rename: must check that the new name is not already used [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] scan the whole list.
- Delete / open an existing file: stop as soon as the file is found [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not necessarily a full scan.

Answer: Creation of a new file, Renaming of an existing file

questions.question:
In the context of schema normalization in relational DBMS, consider a set [latex]\text{F}[/latex] of functional dependencies. The set of all functional dependencies implied by [latex]\text{F}[/latex] is called the closure of [latex]\text{F}[/latex]. To compute the closure of [latex]\text{F}[/latex], Armstrong's Axioms can be applied. Consider [latex]X, Y[/latex], and [latex]Z[/latex] as sets of attributes over a relational schema. The three rules of Armstrong's Axioms are described as follows.

Reflexivity: If [latex]Y \subseteq X[/latex], then [latex]X \rightarrow Y[/latex]
Augmentation: If [latex]X \rightarrow Y[/latex], then [latex]X Z \rightarrow Y Z[/latex] for any Z
Transitivity: If [latex]X \rightarrow Y[/latex] and [latex]Y \rightarrow Z[/latex], then [latex]X \rightarrow Z[/latex]

The additional rule of Union is defined as follows.

Union: If [latex]X \rightarrow Y[/latex] and [latex]X \rightarrow Z[/latex], then [latex]X \rightarrow Y Z[/latex]

It can be proved that the additional rule of Union is also implied by the three rules of Armstrong's Axioms. Listed below are four combinations of these three rules. Which one of these combinations is both necessary and sufficient for the proof?
questions.explanation:
The standard proof of the Union rule ([latex]X\to Y,\,X\to Z\;\Rightarrow\;X\to YZ[/latex]) proceeds as follows:

1. [latex]X\to Y[/latex] (given). By Augmentation (adding [latex]X[/latex] to both sides): [latex]X\to XY[/latex] (using [latex]XX=X[/latex]).
2. [latex]X\to Z[/latex] (given). By Augmentation (adding [latex]Y[/latex] to both sides): [latex]XY\to YZ[/latex].
3. Combining steps 1 and 2 via Transitivity: [latex]X\to XY[/latex] and [latex]XY\to YZ[/latex] gives [latex]X\to YZ[/latex].

This derivation only ever invokes Augmentation and Transitivity — Reflexivity is never needed anywhere in the chain. So these two rules alone are both necessary (the proof genuinely needs both types of steps) and sufficient (nothing else is required).

Answer: Augmentation and Transitivity

questions.question: Consider a relational table R that is in 3NF, but not in BCNF. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?

options.A: R has a nontrivial functional dependency [latex]X\rightarrow A[/latex], where X is not a superkey and A is a prime attribute.
options.B: R has a nontrivial functional dependency [latex]X\rightarrow A[/latex], where X is not a superkey and A is a non-prime attribute and X is not a proper subset of any key.
options.C: R has a nontrivial functional dependency [latex]X\rightarrow A[/latex], where X is not a superkey and A is a non-prime attribute and X is a proper subset of some key.
options.D: A cell in R holds a set instead of an atomic value.

questions.explanation:
3NF allows [latex]X\rightarrow A[/latex] with X not a superkey only when A is a prime attribute. BCNF forbids it.

So a relation in 3NF but not in BCNF must have such an FD with prime A. The other options describe 3NF/2NF violations or a 1NF violation.

Answer: X [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] A where X is not a superkey and A is a prime attribute

questions.question:
Let S be the following schedule of operations of three transactions [latex]T_1, T_2 \text{ and }T_3[/latex] in a relational database system:

[latex]R_2(Y), R_1(X), R_3(Z), R_1(Y)W_1(X), R_2(Z), W_2(Y), R_3(X), W_3(Z)[/latex]

Consider the statements P and Q below:

P: S is conflict-serializable.
Q: If [latex]T_3[/latex] commits before [latex]T_1[/latex] finishes, then S is recoverable.

Which one of the following choices is correct?

options.A: Both P and Q are true
options.B: P is true and Q is false
options.C: P is false and Q is true
options.D: Both P and Q are false

questions.explanation:
Conflicts:
- [latex]R_1(Y)[/latex] before [latex]W_2(Y)[/latex]: T1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T2
- [latex]W_1(X)[/latex] before [latex]R_3(X)[/latex]: T1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T3
- [latex]R_2(Z)[/latex] before [latex]W_3(Z)[/latex]: T2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T3
No cycle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] conflict serializable (T1, T2, T3). P is true.

T3 reads X written by T1. If T3 commits before T1, and T1 later aborts, T3 cannot be undone [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not recoverable. Q is false.

Answer: P is true and Q is false
